source.primary_manuscript: Codex Vaticanus (B/03; Vatican Library Gr. 1209, 4th c. CE ~325-350)
source.primary_manuscript_contains: Essentially complete New Testament; complete Luke
source.secondary_manuscript: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01; British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments, 4th c. CE ~330-360)
source.early_papyri_cross_collation: P75 (Papyrus Bodmer XIV-XV; late 2nd / early 3rd c. CE; Vatican Library, formerly Bodmer Library) preserves substantial portions of Luke including Luke 21 — P75 readings substantially agree with Vaticanus, providing 2nd/3rd-c. confirmation for the Olivet Discourse Greek. P45 (Chester Beatty I; 3rd c. CE) also preserves portions of Luke.
source.reference_critical_apparatus: NA28 (Nestle-Aland 28th, 2012); UBS5 (United Bible Societies 5th, 2014); SBLGNT (SBL 2010); THGNT (Tyndale House 2017)
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly Koine Greek transliteration (SBL convention): polytonic-stripped lowercase Latin with diacritics for breathings (h- for rough; nothing for smooth) and Greek-specific letters (ē for eta, ō for omega, ph for phi, ch for chi, ps for psi, th for theta, rh for rho with rough breathing); ai/ei/oi/au/eu/ou diphthongs preserved; accent marks generally omitted in scholarly translit
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + P75 + P45 original codicology + the NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical apparatus
source.fetchedFrom: SBLGNT public-domain edition (Holmes 2010) + NA28 reference + P75 readings per Bodmer Papyri editions.
source.citation: Aland, Aland, Karavidopoulos, Martini, Metzger, eds., *Novum Testamentum Graece*, 28th ed. (Nestle-Aland, Stuttgart 2012). UBS5 = Aland et al., *The Greek New Testament*, 5th ed. (United Bible Societies 2014). Holmes, M. W., ed., *The Greek New Testament: SBL Edition* (SBL 2010; public-domain). Jongkind, D., ed., *The Greek New Testament*, Tyndale House (Crossway 2017). Codex Vaticanus: Vatican Library Gr. 1209 (4th c.). Codex Sinaiticus: British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg (4th c.). P75 = Papyrus Bodmer XIV-XV (late 2nd / early 3rd c. CE; Vatican Library). Fitzmyer AB 1981-1985; Bovon Hermeneia 2002-2013; Marshall NIGTC 1978; Nolland WBC 1989-1993; Bock BECNT 1994-1996; Green NICNT 1997; Levine-Brettler JANT 2017; Wright *Jesus and the Victory of God* (Fortress 1996) on the Olivet Discourse.
source.paleography_note: The Koine Greek text is preserved in polytonic form as transmitted via SBLGNT. P75's pre-Vaticanus confirmation is particularly important for Luke. The early Greek manuscripts use scriptio continua. Nomina sacra appear abbreviated in the uncials.

verses.text: Ἀναβλέψας δὲ εἶδεν τοὺς βάλλοντας εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον τὰ δῶρα αὐτῶν πλουσίους.
verses.translit: Anablepsas de eiden tous ballontas eis to gazophylakion ta dōra autōn plousious.
verses.notes: TEMPLE-COURT SETTING — the *gazophylakion* (treasury) of the Jerusalem Temple, in the Court of the Women, with its thirteen trumpet-shaped offering chests (m. Šeqalim 6:5). Opening of the widow's-mite pericope. Fitzmyer AB 1320-1321.

verses.text: εἶδεν δέ τινα χήραν πενιχρὰν βάλλουσαν ἐκεῖ λεπτὰ δύο,
verses.translit: eiden de tina chēran penichran ballousan ekei lepta dyo,
verses.notes: *lepta dyo* = two lepta — the smallest Judean copper coin (Mark 12:42 glosses as *kodrantēs*, a Roman quadrans). Penichran (poor) is a hapax in NT.

verses.text: καὶ εἶπεν· Ἀληθῶς λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἡ χήρα αὕτη ἡ πτωχὴ πλεῖον πάντων ἔβαλεν·
verses.translit: kai eipen· Alēthōs legō hymin hoti hē chēra hautē hē ptōchē pleion pantōn ebalen·
verses.notes: The widow's-mite saying. Parallel Mark 12:43-44. *plēion pantōn* (more than all) — the proportional-giving valuation.

verses.text: πάντες γὰρ οὗτοι ἐκ τοῦ περισσεύοντος αὐτοῖς ἔβαλον εἰς τὰ δῶρα, αὕτη δὲ ἐκ τοῦ ὑστερήματος αὐτῆς πάντα τὸν βίον ὃν εἶχεν ἔβαλεν.
verses.translit: pantes gar houtoi ek tou perisseuontos autois ebalon eis ta dōra, hautē de ek tou hysterēmatos autēs panta ton bion hon eichen ebalen.
verses.notes: The *bios* (life / livelihood) given. The pericope thematically transitions to the Temple-destruction prophecy (v.5ff.) — possibly an implicit critique of the Temple-economy that consumes widows' livelihoods (cf. 20:47).

verses.text: Καί τινων λεγόντων περὶ τοῦ ἱεροῦ, ὅτι λίθοις καλοῖς καὶ ἀναθήμασιν κεκόσμηται, εἶπεν·
verses.translit: Kai tinōn legontōn peri tou hierou, hoti lithois kalois kai anathēmasin kekosmētai, eipen·
verses.notes: OLIVET DISCOURSE OPENING. The *anathēmata* (votive offerings) of the Herodian Temple — Josephus *War* 5.5 describes the gold-plated facade and Herod's dedications. The praise of the Temple sets up the destruction-prophecy.

verses.text: Ταῦτα ἃ θεωρεῖτε, ἐλεύσονται ἡμέραι ἐν αἷς οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται λίθος ἐπὶ λίθῳ ὃς οὐ καταλυθήσεται.
verses.translit: Tauta ha theōreite, eleusontai hēmerai en hais ouk aphethēsetai lithos epi lithō hos ou katalythēsetai.
verses.notes: **TEMPLE-DESTRUCTION PROPHECY**. *lithos epi lithō* (stone upon stone) — vivid demolition image. Cross-corpus Mark 13:2 + Matt 24:2. Historically fulfilled 70 CE by Titus; the dating of Luke depends in part on whether this is read as vaticinium ex eventu (Conzelmann) or genuine pre-70 prophecy (Wright).

verses.text: ἐπηρώτησαν δὲ αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, πότε οὖν ταῦτα ἔσται, καὶ τί τὸ σημεῖον ὅταν μέλλῃ ταῦτα γίνεσθαι;
verses.translit: epērōtēsan de auton legontes· Didaskale, pote oun tauta estai, kai ti to sēmeion hotan mellē tauta ginesthai?
verses.notes: The disciples' two-fold question: WHEN + WHAT SIGN. Lukan compression of the Markan two-part private question (Mark 13:3-4). The *sēmeion* (sign) framing structures the discourse.

verses.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Βλέπετε μὴ πλανηθῆτε· πολλοὶ γὰρ ἐλεύσονται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου λέγοντες· Ἐγώ εἰμι, καί· Ὁ καιρὸς ἤγγικεν· μὴ πορευθῆτε ὀπίσω αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: ho de eipen· Blepete mē planēthēte· polloi gar eleusontai epi tō onomati mou legontes· Egō eimi, kai· Ho kairos ēngiken· mē poreuthēte opisō autōn.
verses.notes: FALSE-MESSIAH WARNING. *egō eimi* (I am [he]) — false-messianic claim. *ho kairos ēngiken* (the time has drawn near) — false-imminence claim. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward (a) conventional eschatological-warning reading or (b) Raëlian readings of false-claimant detection; preserve.

verses.text: ὅταν δὲ ἀκούσητε πολέμους καὶ ἀκαταστασίας, μὴ πτοηθῆτε· δεῖ γὰρ ταῦτα γενέσθαι πρῶτον, ἀλλ’ οὐκ εὐθέως τὸ τέλος.
verses.translit: hotan de akousēte polemous kai akatastasias, mē ptoēthēte· dei gar tauta genesthai prōton, all’ ouk eutheōs to telos.
verses.notes: WARS AND DISTURBANCES. *akatastasias* (revolutions / unrest) is Lukan vocabulary (vs. Markan *thoroubous*). The qualifier *ouk eutheōs to telos* (not immediately the end) is a Lukan-distinct delay-of-the-end marker — softening the imminence found in Mark 13:7. Conzelmann's *Theology of St Luke* makes this the centerpiece of Lukan eschatology-by-stages.

verses.text: Τότε ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐγερθήσεται ἔθνος ἐπ’ ἔθνος καὶ βασιλεία ἐπὶ βασιλείαν,
verses.translit: Tote elegen autois· Egerthēsetai ethnos ep’ ethnos kai basileia epi basileian,
verses.notes: Nation-against-nation + kingdom-against-kingdom. Standard apocalyptic-warfare topos. Cross-corpus Isa 19:2; 2 Chr 15:6; 2 Bar 70:3; 4 Ezra 13:31.

verses.text: σεισμοί τε μεγάλοι καὶ κατὰ τόπους λιμοὶ καὶ λοιμοὶ ἔσονται, φόβητρά τε καὶ ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ σημεῖα μεγάλα ἔσται.
verses.translit: seismoi te megaloi kai kata topous limoi kai loimoi esontai, phobētra te kai ap’ ouranou sēmeia megala estai.
verses.notes: **MAJOR COSMIC-SIGNS / EARTH-DISTURBANCES VERSE**. *seismoi* (earthquakes) + *limoi* (famines) + *loimoi* (plagues) — the *limoi kai loimoi* paronomasia is famous (cf. Hesiod *Works and Days* 243). *phobētra* (terrors) is hapax in NT. *ap’ ouranou sēmeia megala* (great signs from heaven) — Luke uniquely adds the heavenly-signs forecast here (Mark 13:8 has only earthquakes+famines). Cross-corpus Joel 2:30 (3:3 LXX); cf. Acts 2:19-20 (the Pentecost Joel-citation). **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward Raëlian readings of *ap’ ouranou sēmeia* (signs from the sky / craft-sightings); preserve the apocalyptic surface.

verses.text: πρὸ δὲ τούτων πάντων ἐπιβαλοῦσιν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῶν καὶ διώξουσιν, παραδιδόντες εἰς τὰς συναγωγὰς καὶ φυλακάς, ἀπαγομένους ἐπὶ βασιλεῖς καὶ ἡγεμόνας ἕνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματός μου·
verses.translit: pro de toutōn pantōn epibalousin eph’ hymas tas cheiras autōn kai diōxousin, paradidontes eis tas synagōgas kai phylakas, apagomenous epi basileis kai hēgemonas heneken tou onomatos mou·
verses.notes: PERSECUTION-FORECAST. *pro de toutōn pantōn* (before all these things) — Lukan ordering signal: persecution PRECEDES the cosmic signs. Foreshadows Acts (synagogue+prison+kings+governors — fulfilled in Acts 4-5; 12; 16; 23-26). Cf. Acts 25-26 (Paul before Felix, Festus, Agrippa).

verses.text: ἀποβήσεται ὑμῖν εἰς μαρτύριον.
verses.translit: apobēsetai hymin eis martyrion.
verses.notes: *eis martyrion* — testimony. Persecution recoded as witness-opportunity (cf. Phil 1:12-14).

verses.text: θέτε οὖν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν μὴ προμελετᾶν ἀπολογηθῆναι,
verses.translit: thete oun en tais kardiais hymōn mē promeletan apologēthēnai,
verses.notes: *promeletan* (premeditate / prepare-in-advance) — rhetorical-technical term for forensic preparation. *apologēthēnai* = give defense. Lukan distinctive saying.

verses.text: ἐγὼ γὰρ δώσω ὑμῖν στόμα καὶ σοφίαν ᾗ οὐ δυνήσονται ἀντιστῆναι ἢ ἀντειπεῖν πάντες οἱ ἀντικείμενοι ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: egō gar dōsō hymin stoma kai sophian hē ou dynēsontai antistēnai ē anteipein pantes hoi antikeimenoi hymin.
verses.notes: Divine-rhetoric promise. Cross-corpus Exod 4:12 (Yahweh to Moses); cf. Acts 6:10 (Stephen's wisdom). Lukan substitution: Mark/Matt have the Holy Spirit speaking; Luke has the risen-Christ giving wisdom directly.

verses.text: παραδοθήσεσθε δὲ καὶ ὑπὸ γονέων καὶ ἀδελφῶν καὶ συγγενῶν καὶ φίλων, καὶ θανατώσουσιν ἐξ ὑμῶν,
verses.translit: paradothēsesthe de kai hypo goneōn kai adelphōn kai syngenōn kai philōn, kai thanatōsousin ex hymōn,
verses.notes: Family-betrayal forecast. *thanatōsousin ex hymōn* (they will put some of you to death) — martyrdom-forecast. Cross-corpus Mic 7:6; Mark 13:12; Matt 10:21.

verses.text: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου.
verses.translit: kai esesthe misoumenoi hypo pantōn dia to onoma mou.
verses.notes: Universal-hostility forecast. *dia to onoma mou* (because of my name) — formulaic NT persecution-cause.

verses.text: καὶ θρὶξ ἐκ τῆς κεφαλῆς ὑμῶν οὐ μὴ ἀπόληται.
verses.translit: kai thrix ek tēs kephalēs hymōn ou mē apolētai.
verses.notes: *thrix ek tēs kephalēs* (a hair from the head) — proverbial-protection saying (cross-corpus 1 Sam 14:45; 2 Sam 14:11; 1 Kgs 1:52; Acts 27:34). The tension with v.16 (some put to death) suggests a spiritual rather than physical preservation.

verses.text: ἐν τῇ ὑπομονῇ ὑμῶν κτήσασθε τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: en tē hypomonē hymōn ktēsasthe tas psychas hymōn.
verses.notes: **MAJOR THEME — ENDURANCE**. *hypomonē* (endurance) + *ktēsasthe tas psychas* (gain your souls/lives). Variant: NA28/SBLGNT read *ktēsasthe* (aorist imperative); some witnesses read *ktēsesthe* (future indicative — "you will gain"). Lukan re-coding of Mark 13:13b *ho de hypomeinas eis telos houtos sōthēsetai*.

verses.text: Ὅταν δὲ ἴδητε κυκλουμένην ὑπὸ στρατοπέδων Ἰερουσαλήμ, τότε γνῶτε ὅτι ἤγγικεν ἡ ἐρήμωσις αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: Hotan de idēte kykloumenēn hypo stratopedōn Ierousalēm, tote gnōte hoti ēngiken hē erēmōsis autēs.
verses.notes: **LUKAN DISTINCTIVE — JERUSALEM ENCIRCLEMENT**. Where Mark 13:14 has the cryptic *bdelygma tēs erēmōseōs* (abomination of desolation; cf. Dan 9:27), Luke unveils the apocalyptic cipher as historical military encirclement — the 70 CE Roman siege under Titus. The Lukan demythologization is a major argument for post-70 dating (Fitzmyer; Conzelmann), though Wright argues for pre-70 prophetic specificity. *stratopeda* = army-camps.

verses.text: τότε οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ φευγέτωσαν εἰς τὰ ὄρη, καὶ οἱ ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῆς ἐκχωρείτωσαν, καὶ οἱ ἐν ταῖς χώραις μὴ εἰσερχέσθωσαν εἰς αὐτήν,
verses.translit: tote hoi en tē Ioudaia pheugetōsan eis ta orē, kai hoi en mesō autēs ekchōreitōsan, kai hoi en tais chōrais mē eiserchesthōsan eis autēn,
verses.notes: Flight-to-the-mountains command. Eusebius *HE* 3.5.3 reports the Jerusalem Christians fled to Pella (Transjordan) before the siege — possibly fulfillment-tradition shaped by this saying.

verses.text: ὅτι ἡμέραι ἐκδικήσεως αὗταί εἰσιν τοῦ πλησθῆναι πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα.
verses.translit: hoti hēmerai ekdikēseōs hautai eisin tou plēsthēnai panta ta gegrammena.
verses.notes: *hēmerai ekdikēseōs* (days of vengeance) — cross-corpus Hos 9:7. Lukan-distinctive prophecy-fulfillment frame: *plēsthēnai panta ta gegrammena* (all that is written to be fulfilled).

verses.text: οὐαὶ ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις καὶ ταῖς θηλαζούσαις ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις· ἔσται γὰρ ἀνάγκη μεγάλη ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ὀργὴ τῷ λαῷ τούτῳ,
verses.translit: ouai tais en gastri echousais kai tais thēlazousais en ekeinais tais hēmerais· estai gar anankē megalē epi tēs gēs kai orgē tō laō toutō,
verses.notes: Woe-saying on pregnant + nursing women. *anankē megalē* (great distress). *orgē tō laō toutō* (wrath upon this people) — Lukan-distinctive specification (Mark has *thlipsis* without ethnic specification).

verses.text: καὶ πεσοῦνται στόματι μαχαίρης καὶ αἰχμαλωτισθήσονται εἰς τὰ ἔθνη πάντα, καὶ Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἔσται πατουμένη ὑπὸ ἐθνῶν, ἄχρι οὗ πληρωθῶσιν καιροὶ ἐθνῶν.
verses.translit: kai pesountai stomati machairēs kai aichmalōtisthēsontai eis ta ethnē panta, kai Ierousalēm estai patoumenē hypo ethnōn, achri hou plērōthōsin kairoi ethnōn.
verses.notes: **LUKAN DISTINCTIVE — *kairoi ethnōn* (times of the Gentiles)**. The phrase is unique to Luke and load-bearing for Lukan salvation-historical scheme (Conzelmann's Mitte der Zeit). *patoumenē* (trampled) — cross-corpus Zech 12:3 LXX; Dan 8:13. Cross-corpus Rom 11:25 (the Pauline *plērōma tōn ethnōn*). The siege-trampling forecast was historically fulfilled 70 CE and again 135 CE (Bar Kokhba).

verses.text: Καὶ ἔσονται σημεῖα ἐν ἡλίῳ καὶ σελήνῃ καὶ ἄστροις, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς συνοχὴ ἐθνῶν ἐν ἀπορίᾳ ἤχους θαλάσσης καὶ σάλου,
verses.translit: Kai esontai sēmeia en hēliō kai selēnē kai astrois, kai epi tēs gēs synochē ethnōn en aporia ēchous thalassēs kai salou,
verses.notes: **MAJOR COSMIC-SIGNS VERSE — RAËLIAN CANON CITATION SITE**. *sēmeia en hēliō kai selēnē kai astrois* (signs in sun and moon and stars). Cross-corpus Joel 2:30-31 (3:3-4 LXX); Isa 13:10; Ezek 32:7-8; cf. Acts 2:19-20 (Peter's Pentecost Joel-citation); Rev 6:12-13. **RAËLIAN CANON CITATION**: this verse is engaged in Raël *The End of the World*. Flag for Editor; acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework applies. **PHILOLOGICALLY**: *synochē* (anguish / distress); *aporia* (perplexity); *ēchos* (roar); *salos* (tossing / surge). The seismic + maritime + cosmic distress-catalogue is dense. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward (a) conventional apocalyptic-tradition reading or (b) Raëlian end-time / cosmic-sign reading.

verses.text: ἀποψυχόντων ἀνθρώπων ἀπὸ φόβου καὶ προσδοκίας τῶν ἐπερχομένων τῇ οἰκουμένῃ, αἱ γὰρ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν σαλευθήσονται.
verses.translit: apopsychontōn anthrōpōn apo phobou kai prosdokias tōn eperchomenōn tē oikoumenē, hai gar dynameis tōn ouranōn saleuthēsontai.
verses.notes: **COSMIC-SIGNS CONTINUED**. *apopsychontōn* (fainting / expiring) — vivid hapax in NT. *hai dynameis tōn ouranōn* (the powers of the heavens) — cross-corpus Isa 34:4 LXX; Hag 2:6 LXX; cf. Heb 12:26. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: *dynameis tōn ouranōn* is sometimes read in heterodox traditions (including the Raëlian canon's *The End of the World*) as referring to celestial beings/craft; the dominant scholarly reading is to celestial bodies/cosmic order. Preserve.

verses.text: καὶ τότε ὄψονται τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐν νεφέλῃ μετὰ δυνάμεως καὶ δόξης πολλῆς.
verses.translit: kai tote opsontai ton huion tou anthrōpou erchomenon en nephelē meta dynameōs kai doxēs pollēs.
verses.notes: **MAJOR SON-OF-MAN VERSE — DANIELIC PAROUSIA**. *ton huion tou anthrōpou erchomenon en nephelē* (the Son of Man coming in a cloud) — direct cross-corpus to **Dan 7:13-14** LXX/Th (*meta tōn nephelōn tou ouranou hōs huios anthrōpou ērcheto*). Singular *nephelē* (Luke) vs. plural *nephelais* (Mark 13:26; Matt 24:30) — Lukan stylistic touch, possibly assimilating to Acts 1:9 (*nephelē hypelaben auton*) the ascension-cloud. **MAJOR LENS-RISK SITE**: the *en nephelē* (in a cloud) descent-image is heavily engaged in the Raëlian canon (*The Book Which Tells the Truth*; *The End of the World*) as Elohim-craft / Vimana-style aerial vehicle. Flag for Editor. Acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework applies. **EDITOR DO NOT PRE-RESOLVE**: preserve the cloud-image; document the canon-citation in apparatus.

verses.text: ἀρχομένων δὲ τούτων γίνεσθαι ἀνακύψατε καὶ ἐπάρατε τὰς κεφαλὰς ὑμῶν, διότι ἐγγίζει ἡ ἀπολύτρωσις ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: archomenōn de toutōn ginesthai anakypsate kai eparate tas kephalas hymōn, dioti engizei hē apolytrōsis hymōn.
verses.notes: *anakypsate* (straighten up) + *eparate tas kephalas* (raise your heads) — Lukan-distinctive posture-of-hope command (where Mark 13:27 has only the angelic gathering). *apolytrōsis* (redemption / release) — Pauline vocabulary (Rom 3:24; Eph 1:7) but here in dominical mouth.

verses.text: Καὶ εἶπεν παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς· Ἴδετε τὴν συκῆν καὶ πάντα τὰ δένδρα·
verses.translit: Kai eipen parabolēn autois· Idete tēn sykēn kai panta ta dendra·
verses.notes: Fig-tree parable. Lukan universalization: *kai panta ta dendra* (and all the trees) — Luke broadens from Mark 13:28's fig-tree only.

verses.text: ὅταν προβάλωσιν ἤδη, βλέποντες ἀφ’ ἑαυτῶν γινώσκετε ὅτι ἤδη ἐγγὺς τὸ θέρος ἐστίν·
verses.translit: hotan probalōsin ēdē, blepontes aph’ heautōn ginōskete hoti ēdē engys to theros estin·
verses.notes: *probalōsin* (put forth [leaves]). *theros* (summer / harvest).

verses.text: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ἴδητε ταῦτα γινόμενα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγύς ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: houtōs kai hymeis, hotan idēte tauta ginomena, ginōskete hoti engys estin hē basileia tou theou.
verses.notes: **KINGDOM-IMMINENCE FORMULA**. *engys estin hē basileia tou theou* — Lukan re-coding (where Mark 13:29 has only *engys estin epi thyrais* without specifying the kingdom). Major Lukan kingdom-theme echo (cf. 10:9, 11; 11:20; 17:21).

verses.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται.
verses.translit: amēn legō hymin hoti ou mē parelthē hē genea hautē heōs an panta genētai.
verses.notes: **MAJOR THEOLOGICAL-INTERPRETIVE CRUX — *hē genea hautē* ("this generation")**. The eschatological-imminence saying. Interpretive options surveyed by Marshall NIGTC 779-780 + Fitzmyer AB 1353: (a) Jesus' literal contemporaries — supporting the consistent-eschatology / Schweitzer reading that Jesus was mistaken about imminence; (b) the Jewish people as race / generation-type; (c) the wicked-generation typology (Deut 32:5); (d) the generation witnessing the signs. Cross-corpus Mark 13:30; Matt 24:34. **HIGH LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward (a) skeptical 'failed prophecy' reading, (b) preterist 'fulfilled in 70 CE' reading, (c) futurist reading, or (d) Raëlian readings; preserve the crux. **EDITOR DO NOT PRE-RESOLVE.**

verses.text: ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ παρελεύσονται, οἱ δὲ λόγοι μου οὐ μὴ παρελεύσονται.
verses.translit: ho ouranos kai hē gē pareleusontai, hoi de logoi mou ou mē pareleusontai.
verses.notes: Word-of-Jesus-permanence saying. Cross-corpus Isa 40:8 + 51:6. The contrast with the imminence-saying of v.32 is structurally striking.

verses.text: Προσέχετε δὲ ἑαυτοῖς μήποτε βαρηθῶσιν ὑμῶν αἱ καρδίαι ἐν κραιπάλῃ καὶ μέθῃ καὶ μερίμναις βιωτικαῖς, καὶ ἐπιστῇ ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς αἰφνίδιος ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνη
verses.translit: Prosechete de heautois mēpote barēthōsin hymōn hai kardiai en kraipalē kai methē kai merimnais biōtikais, kai epistē eph’ hymas aiphnidios hē hēmera ekeinē
verses.notes: **LUKAN-DISTINCTIVE PARAENESIS**. *kraipalē* (drinking-hangover) + *methē* (drunkenness) + *merimnai biōtikai* (worldly cares) — Hellenistic-moralist vocabulary. *aiphnidios* (sudden) — hapax in NT (cf. 1 Thess 5:3 *aiphnidios autois ephistatai olethros*). The Lukan paraenesis-shift moves the discourse from imminence-interpretation to ethical readiness.

verses.text: ὡς παγίς· ἐπεισελεύσεται γὰρ ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς καθημένους ἐπὶ πρόσωπον πάσης τῆς γῆς.
verses.translit: hōs pagis· epeiseleusetai gar epi pantas tous kathēmenous epi prosōpon pasēs tēs gēs.
verses.notes: *pagis* (snare / trap) — cross-corpus Isa 24:17 LXX. *epi prosōpon pasēs tēs gēs* (upon the face of all the earth) — universalizing scope. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward Raëlian planetary-scope reading.

verses.text: ἀγρυπνεῖτε δὲ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ δεόμενοι ἵνα κατισχύσητε ἐκφυγεῖν ταῦτα πάντα τὰ μέλλοντα γίνεσθαι, καὶ σταθῆναι ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
verses.translit: agrypneite de en panti kairō deomenoi hina katischysēte ekphygein tauta panta ta mellonta ginesthai, kai stathēnai emprosthen tou huiou tou anthrōpou.
verses.notes: **MAJOR ESCHATOLOGICAL-WATCHFULNESS SAYING**. *agrypneite* (be alert / sleepless). *katischysēte ekphygein* (be able to escape) — variant: NA28/SBLGNT read *katischysēte*; some witnesses read *kataxiōthēte* ("be counted worthy"). The two readings have different soteriological-effort implications; the *katischysēte* reading (modern critical) emphasizes empowerment-to-escape; the *kataxiōthēte* (Byzantine/Textus Receptus) emphasizes worthiness-judgment. *stathēnai emprosthen tou huiou tou anthrōpou* (to stand before the Son of Man) — final-judgment scene. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: preserve.

verses.text: Ἦν δὲ τὰς ἡμέρας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ διδάσκων, τὰς δὲ νύκτας ἐξερχόμενος ηὐλίζετο εἰς τὸ ὄρος τὸ καλούμενον Ἐλαιῶν·
verses.translit: Ēn de tas hēmeras en tō hierō didaskōn, tas de nyktas exerchomenos ēulizeto eis to oros to kaloumenon Elaiōn·
verses.notes: Daily routine: teaching in Temple by day, lodging on Mount of Olives by night. *Elaiōn* (of olives) — Olivet name. Lukan summary preparing the Passion Narrative.

verses.text: καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ὤρθριζεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai pas ho laos ōrthrizen pros auton en tō hierō akouein autou.
verses.notes: *ōrthrizen* (got up early) — populace's eagerness. Chapter-closing summary. Some Western witnesses + early Latin insert the Pericope Adulterae (John 7:53-8:11) AFTER Luke 21:38 in some witnesses (one of the floating-pericope locations) — documented in apparatus but not reproduced here.
